content.title: About
content.content: Fried perch is a freshwater fish from the perch family, cooked on a skillet or in the oven until a golden crust forms. It has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture thanks to the browned exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Perch inhabits fresh and slightly brackish waters across the Northern Hemisphere.
Frying retains most B‑vitamins, which are important for metabolism.
Traditionally, perch is fried in butter with lemon and herbs such as dill or parsley.
In some cuisines, fried perch is considered a delicacy and is served in upscale restaurants.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Perch provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA support heart health, vascular function, and brain performance.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Perch supplies selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, important for metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Low mercury content
items.content: Compared with large predatory fish, perch contains less mercury, making it safer for regular consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including perch.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Frying in abundant oil significantly increases the dish’s calorie density.

items.title: Possible contaminants
items.content: Although low in mercury, water may contain other pollutants; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried perch can be served hot as a main course with vegetable, potato, or rice sides. It pairs well with lemon juice, butter sauce, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fried perch in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.
